title: Jacobian-normalized dualizing datum of a relative nodal curve
statement: Let $p:Y\to T$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. A regular affine curve presentation consists of affine opens $U\subset Y$, $V\subset T$ with $p(U)\subset V$, an integer $c\ge0$, a surjection $q:R[x_0,\ldots,x_c]\to B$ with $R=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_T)$, $B=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_Y)$, whose coefficient map is induced by $p$, and an ordered regular sequence $f_1,\ldots,f_c$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] generating its kernel. A nodal dualizing datum on an $\mathcal O_Y$-module $\omega$ consists of invertibility [def-sc-invertible-module], a fundamental-class morphism $\alpha:\Omega^1_{Y/T}\to\omega$ (relative differentials are [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]), coverage of $Y$ by such presentations, and the following normalization in every such presentation. There is a $B$-linear isomorphism $e:\Gamma(U,\omega)\simeq B$ such that, for every polynomial $a$, $e(\alpha(dq(a)))=q(\det(\partial(f_1,\ldots,f_c,a)/\partial(x_0,\ldots,x_c)))$. In addition, for the immersion $i:U\to\operatorname{Spec}R[x_0,\ldots,x_c]$ one has $i_*(\omega|_U)\simeq\mathcal Ext^c(i_*\mathcal O_U,\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-pbc-sheaf-ext], with the second argument identified with the top relative differential module by the ordered coordinate volume form; restriction uses [def-pc-module-pullback]. The Jacobian normalization specifies the adjunction transitions on overlaps, including on a nonseparated source.
